steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Equilibrium price is where supply equals demand — the market clears with no excess.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Excess demand (shortage) occurs below equilibrium — consumers want more than producers supply, pushing price up. Excess supply (surplus) above equilibrium pushes price down.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: An increase in demand raises equilibrium price and quantity. An increase in supply raises quantity but lowers price.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: When both supply and demand shift, the effect on price or quantity depends on relative size of shifts.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain how equilibrium price is determined using a supply and demand diagram. | Using a diagram, show what happens to equilibrium when demand increases but supply is unchanged. | Analyse how a poor wheat harvest would affect bread price, quantity, and producer revenue.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always draw diagrams with BOTH curves, clearly labelling original and new equilibrium (P,Q → P1,Q1). When both curves shift, state that one variable's direction is INDETERMINATE without knowing relative magnitudes. Link revenue to elasticity: price rise + inelastic demand = higher revenue; price rise + elastic demand = lower revenue.
